simple.meaning: מִגְרָשׁ (migrâsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a suburb (i.e. open country whither flocks are driven from pasture); hence, the area around a building , or the margin of the sea.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 115 times across Leviticus, Numbers, Joshua, 1 Chronicles, beginning at Leviticus 25:34. Its contexts include city, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִגְרָשׁ (H4054).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מִגְרָשׁ (migrâsh) / H4054 is traced through Leviticus 25:34, Numbers 35:2, Numbers 35:3, Numbers 35:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a suburb (i.e. open country whither flocks are driven from pasture); hence, the area around a building , or the margin of the sea
definitions.full: H4054. migrash or migrashah מִגְרָשׁ noun masculine Num 35:2 common, common-land, open land (perhaps originally pasture-land , as place of [cattle] driving ) — absolute ׳מ Ezek 45:2 2 t. + 48:15 (Co מגרשָׁהּ ); construct מִגְרַשׁ Lev 25:34 ; 2Chr 31:19 ; (on מִגְרָשָׁהּ Ezek 36:5 compare גרשׁ ); elsewhere plural, absolute מִגְרשׁוֺת 27:28 (Baer); Co מרעשׁת assumed from רָעַשׁ , compare ᵐ5 ; construct מִגְרְשֵׁי Num 35:4 2 t.; suffix מִגְרָשֶׁיהָ Josh 21:13 (twice in verse) + 42 t.; מִגְרָשֶׁהָ 21:11 46t. in Joshua 21 (generally ֑ or ֔ + but also ֖ 21:21 ); מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם Num 35:3-4 t.; מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶן 35:7-8 t. — common-land , usually plural, and usually as attached to a city or town, especially as surrounding Levitical cities 35:2-3 , 4 , 5 , 7 ; Josh 14:4 ; 21:2 55t. occurrences.englishText: But the field of the pasture lands of their cities may not be sold, for it is their perpetual possession.
“Command the children of Israel to give to the Levites cities to dwell in out of their inheritance. You shall give pasture lands for the cities around them to the Levites.
They shall have the cities to dwell in. Their pasture lands shall be for their livestock, and for their possessions, and for all their animals.

“The pasture lands of the cities, which you shall give to the Levites, shall be from the wall of the city and outward one thousand cubits* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. around it.

You shall measure outside of the city for the east side two thousand cubits, and for the south side two thousand cubits, and for the west side two thousand cubits, and for the north side two thousand cubits, the city being in the middle. This shall be the pasture lands of their cities.
All the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities together with their pasture lands.

For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and for their property.
They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “Yahweh commanded through Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with their pasture lands for our livestock.”
